title: Project documentation
must: Documents produced in the system life cycle; technical documentation (for programmers: algorithms, data dictionary, ERD, test plan) vs user guide (for users: installation, tasks, error messages) — readers, contents, language, purpose.

title: Why documentation must be well made
must: New developers, users and examiners rely on it; structure matters: TOC → where is the section, header/footer → which document/version/page, footnotes → source or meaning, tables → value for an item.

title: Header and footer
must: Areas in the top and bottom margins repeated on every page; entered once, consistent, keep title and version visible on printed pages.

title: Fields
must: A placeholder the word processor fills in and updates automatically: page number, total pages (Page X of Y), date, file name.

title: What headers and footers contain
must: At least four: title / project name, chapter name, version number and date (why it matters), logo, page number, author, confidentiality notice, file name.

title: Header options and header vs heading
must: Different first page, odd/even pages, sections with their own header (Link to Previous); a header is in the margin and repeated, a heading is in the body, appears once and is used for the TOC.

title: Footnotes and endnotes
must: Footnote: reference mark in the text + note at the bottom of the same page; endnote: notes collected at the end; numbering updates automatically.

title: Uses of footnotes
must: Citing sources (author, title, URL, date — avoids plagiarism), explaining terms, extra detail; footnotes vs endnotes compared (position, reading, best for).

title: Tables and captions
must: Rows and columns of cells for structured data, one fact per cell; a numbered caption ('Table 4. …') so it can be referred to.

title: Tables in project documents
must: At least three with their columns: data dictionary, test plan, schedule, requirements list, troubleshooting, revision history.

title: Good table practice
must: Header row repeated on every page, caption, consistent alignment, simple borders/shading; why a table beats a paragraph (easy to scan, missing values visible).

title: Automatic table of contents
must: Headings with page numbers at the start; generated from heading styles (Heading 1, 2, 3); placed after the title page; Update Table after editing; Ctrl+click jumps to a section.

title: Automatic vs typed TOC
must: Automatic TOC updates headings and page numbers and has hyperlinks; a typed one goes out of date; heading styles also drive the Navigation pane and PDF bookmarks.

title: Common mistakes
must: Typing page numbers or footnote numbers by hand, confusing header with heading, no version number, headings made bold instead of heading styles, not updating the TOC.
